SECTION 1: VETERINARY ANTIBIOTICS - MAXIMUM RESIDUE LIMITS (MRL)
================================================================================

A. SEAFOOD AND FISH PRODUCTS
-----------------------------------
Drug Name                    | Limit      | Food Category          | Notes
-----------------------------------
Tetracycline               | 0.1 mg/kg  | Fish & Fishery Products|
Oxytetracycline            | 0.1 mg/kg  | Fish & Fishery Products|
Trimethoprim               | 0.05 mg/kg | Fish & Fishery Products|
Oxolinic acid              | 0.3 mg/kg  | Fish & Fishery Products|

B. HONEY PRODUCTS
-----------------------------------
Drug Name                    | Limit      | Notes
-----------------------------------
Chloramphenicol            | 0.3 μg/kg  | Limit of Quantification (LOQ)
Nitrofurans & metabolites  | 0.5 μg/kg  | Collectively measured
Sulphonamides & metabolites| 5.0 μg/kg  | Individually/collectively
Streptomycin               | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Tetracycline               | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Oxytetracycline            | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Chlortetracycline          | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Ampicillin                 | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Enrofloxacin               | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Ciprofloxacin              | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Erythromycin               | 5.0 μg/kg  |
Tylosin                    | 5.0 μg/kg  |

Note: Analysis method: LC-MS/MS

E. EXTENDED MRL ANTIBIOTICS
-----------------------------------
- Albendazole (anthelmintic): Muscle 0.1, Liver 5, Kidney 5, Fat 0.1, Milk 0.1 mg/kg
- Closantel: Muscle 1-1.5, Liver 1-1.5, Kidney 3-5, Fat 2-3 mg/kg (Cattle/Sheep)
- Clenbuterol (β2-agonist): Muscle 0.0002-0.0002, Liver 0.0006, Kidney 0.0006 mg/kg
- Doramectin (avermectin): Variable by species (Cattle, Pig)
- Febantel/Fenbendazole/Oxfendazole: Muscle 0.1, Liver 0.5, Kidney 0.1, Fat 0.1 mg/kg
- Ivermectin (avermectin): Milk 0.01, Liver 0.8, Fat 0.4, Muscle 0.03, Kidney 0.1 mg/kg
- Levamisole: Muscle 0.01, Liver 0.1, Kidney 0.01, Fat 0.01 mg/kg
- Moxidectin: Muscle 0.02-0.05, Liver 0.1, Kidney 0.05, Fat 0.5 mg/kg
- Nicarbazin (Chicken): Kidney/Fat/Liver/Muscle each 0.2 mg/kg
- Thiabendazole: Muscle 0.1, Liver 0.1, Kidney 0.1, Fat 0.1, Milk 0.1 mg/L
- Triclabendazole: Muscle 0.2-0.25, Liver 0.3-0.85, Kidney 0.2-0.4, Fat/Skin 0.1 mg/kg
- Diminazene: Muscle 0.5, Liver 12, Kidney 6, Milk 0.15 mg/L (Cattle)

================================================================================
SECTION 2: PROHIBITED VETERINARY DRUGS AND ANTIBIOTICS
================================================================================

EXTRANEOUS MAXIMUM RESIDUE LIMIT (EMRL):
- General substances: 0.001 mg/kg
- Chloramphenicol: 0.0003 mg/kg (0.3 μg/kg)

PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES (Not allowed in meat, poultry, eggs, seafood, fishery products):

1. Nitrofurans group:
   - Furaltadone
   - Furazolidone
   - Nitrofurantoin
   - Nitrofurazone

2. Chloramphenicol (absolute ban in meat/animal products - only 0.3 μg/kg EMRL in honey)

3. Sulphamethoxazole

4. Aristolochia spp and preparations thereof

5. Chloroform

6. Chloropromazine

7. Colchicine

8. Dapsone

9. Dimetridazole

10. Metronidazole

11. Ronidazole

12. Ipronidazole and other nitromidazoles

13. Clenbuterol (except trace residues: 0.0002-0.0006 mg/kg)

14. Diethylstilbestrol (synthetic estrogen)

15. Glycopeptides

16. Stilbenes and other steroids

17. Crystal Violet (dye)

18. Malachite Green (dye)

19. Carbadox

================================================================================
SECTION 5: WITHDRAWAL PERIODS
================================================================================

WITHDRAWAL PERIODS (from FSSAI regulations):

Important Notes:
1. No specific withdrawal periods are explicitly detailed in individual drug sections
2. Manufacturers/Veterinarians must follow:
   - Drug package insert recommendations
   - Regional veterinary standards
   - FSSAI approved veterinary medicine list

3. General principle: Minimum withdrawal period should ensure MRL compliance

Key Categories for Consideration:
- Systemic antibiotics: 3-7 days (typical)
- Macrolide antibiotics: 5-10 days
- Aminoglycosides: 10-14 days
- Beta-lactams: 2-5 days
- Fluoroquinolones: 5-7 days
- Anthelmintics: 7-14 days
- Ionophores: 3-5 days
- Growth promoters: 14-28 days (if permitted)

CRITICAL: Refer to specific product labels and FSSAI-approved veterinary drug list
for actual withdrawal periods compliant with these MRL values.

================================================================================

Aflatoxin Limits (μg/kg):

Food Category                        | Total Aflatoxins | Aflatoxin B1
Cereals and Cereal Products         | 15               | -
Dried Figs                          | 10               | -
Nuts (for further processing)       | 15               | -
Nuts (ready to eat)                 | 15               | -
Oilseeds (for further processing)   | 15               | -
Oilseeds (ready to eat)             | 15               | -
Pulses                              | 15               | -
Spices/Spice Mix                    | 30               | -
Arecanut/Betelnut                   | 10-15            | -

Note: Aflatoxin B1 often limited to 5 μg/kg where specified

================================================================================
SECTION 7: USAGE GUIDELINES FOR FARM MANAGEMENT PORTAL
================================================================================

A. DATA ORGANIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS:

1. By Animal Type:
   - Cattle (Dairy & Beef)
   - Poultry (Chicken, Turkey, Duck)
   - Pigs
   - Sheep & Goats
   - Aquaculture (Fish, Prawns)
   - Honey Production

2. By Tissue Type:
   - Muscle/Meat
   - Liver
   - Kidney
   - Fat/Adipose Tissue
   - Milk
   - Eggs
   - Honey

3. By Drug Class:
   - Antibiotics (Beta-lactams, Macrolides, etc.)
   - Antiparasitics (Anthelmintics, Antiprotozoals)
   - Anti-inflammatories
   - Ionophores
   - Fluoroquinolones

B. CRITICAL COMPLIANCE POINTS:

1. Always check food category specificity - same drug may have different MRL
2. Note tissue-specific limits for kidney and liver (often higher than muscle)
3. Milk typically has lowest MRL values
4. Some substances have ZERO tolerance (absolute prohibition)
5. Regularly update to latest FSSAI amendments
6. Maintain withdrawal period log for animals

C. CONTAMINANT MONITORING:

1. Regular testing required for:
   - Heavy metals (especially in seafood)
   - Pesticide residues (especially in crops)
   - Antibiotic residues (in animal products)
   - Aflatoxins (in grains, nuts, spices)

2. Testing frequency should reflect:
   - Production scale
   - Product category risk
   - Historical compliance
